why: The import edge is a dependency edge the scanner should get. The DI wiring in beans.xml is a dependency the container creates at runtime — recordable, never scannable.

ground_truth_revisions.why: The classification was wrong, and implementing a pom reader is what proved it. pom.xml declares spring-core for the PROJECT. It does not — cannot — say which Java package uses it, and in this fixture OrderService.java imports only com.acme.billing. Producing `com/acme/order -> ext:spring-core` therefore requires PICKING a package, which is invention, not resolution. Calling that `manifest` difficulty told a reader the scanner was leaving free accuracy on the table; it was not.
ground_truth_revisions.honesty_note: This was the last miss in the `manifest` band and reclassifying it takes that band to 100%. That is exactly the move that makes a harness worthless, so state the test plainly: a pom reader WAS implemented in the same commit (multi-module poms now emit their own dependencies), it was pointed at this fixture, and it correctly declines to attribute a root pom's dependency to a package. The number moved because the classification was wrong, not to make the number move. The edge stays in the corpus, still unfound, in a band that says why it will stay that way.
